This separation is enforced by cortical resistance mechanisms—both intrinsic and extrinsic—that maintain perceptual fidelity. When resistance fails (e.g., due to low T or high D), neural disintegration allows hallucinatory states to emerge. The dual nature of resistance implies a layered control system: one that stabilizes cognition through cohesion and another that modulates external influence. These dynamics form a bifurcation structure in cognitive state space, where sensory input acts as a control parameter. Hallucinations occur when the system crosses a critical threshold in this space, driven by internal or external perturbations. The mathematical framework thus models cognition as a hybrid deterministic-stochastic dynamical system, governed by activation thresholds and resistance profiles.
